answer: Sybil resistance works when an agent's identity is priced per action, not per keypair. A new agent joins an atlas of bonded identities and stakes value any challenger can seize if its claims fail an audit. Verification is cheap, claiming is not: a forger must fund each clone and keep it credible through inspection, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand stakes plus compute. Reputation accrues only on settled work, so fresh keys start at zero trust. Records stack like timber rings, each verified round adding an unfakeable one, and ferrous dispute deposits make fraud costly to start and abandon.
